Jonas / Ben — tagging in what we can commit to for the pilot and proposed language. Summary below; I can produce a one-page addendum for signature once we agree final wording.

- Controller vs Processor: Redwood will accept the role of processor for processing Acme-originated datasets for the pilot. We will include standard DSR (data subject request) cooperation language: Redwood will surface requests received about processing it performs and will assist Acme within a reasonable timeframe (typically 5 business days) to facilitate DSR responses. Suggested sample clause: "Redwood Inference acts as Processor for Customer Data and will, at Customer's direction, assist in responding to Data Subject Requests to the extent applicable to the processing performed by Redwood."

- Subprocessor notification: For the pilot we can provide a 30-calendar-day notice window prior to onboarding any subprocessor that could access production data. For standard enterprise contracts we normally publish changes to our subprocessor list and provide 14-day notice; offering 30 days for this pilot is an exception we can make but will be captured only in the pilot addendum. Proposed wording for addendum: "Redwood will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) calendar days' prior notice before adding any new subprocessor that may access Customer's production data for the Pilot."

- Data residency & backups: We can confirm that production datasets marked as EU-resident will remain physically located in EU regions for the duration of the pilot. Backups of EU-resident production data will also be stored in EU-only storage by default. Note: if Acme requests cross-region replication for specific test cases, that will be scoped and require an exception.

- Logs & retention: Default telemetry and audit logs are retained for 90 days. Request/response content used for model input is redacted by default after processing unless a customer explicitly opts into longer retention for debug (this must be approved in writing). KV cache: session-level KV cache is ephemeral and maintained only for the duration of active sessions; we do persist model-state caches for warm-start efficiency but they are not used to reconstruct PII and are covered by the same retention policy. We can offer a 180-day retention option for audit logs by addendum for the pilot if needed (note: increases cost).

Next steps I recommend: Jonas prepare a one-page pilot addendum template, we mark the subprocessor notice window and EU residency clauses as pilot-only, and Ben include indicated retention options in the commercial proposal. I’ll draft the precise clauses and send a PR to Jonas for signature-ready language by EOD tomorrow.
